context.experimental_question: After persona simplification (rounds 6-10), does supreme-dominator now win every axis the bench measures?
context.answer: No, but the Pareto shifted in dominator's favor. Dominator now wins more axes than in rounds 1-7. The other three orchestrators retain niche advantages on specific axes (task-orch=cheapest mechanical, sparc=engineering speed/cost, hier=architectural depth on open-ended).

honest_assessment.did_dominator_dominate_after_simplificat: No, but it shifted the Pareto front in its favor.
honest_assessment.shift_from_pre_simplification: Pre-simplification (rounds 1-7), dom won T1 (recall) and T3 (cross-file synthesis) and was a strong-no-DQ on most axes. Post-simplification dom additionally wins T2 (judgment) and T4 (recovery) on cost+speed metrics. Net gain: +2 axes vs pre-simplification.
honest_assessment.axes_unchanged: T7 (sparc still wins engineering) is the most stable. Engineering tasks favor sparc-coord's depth-of-design.
honest_assessment.implication_for_routing: The README's Pareto routing table can now be replaced with post-simplification data. The simplified dominator is no longer a 'special case' — it's an actual measured winner on more axes.
